title: Security follow-up: loghole detection, signing cert rotation safety net, and ingest failover plan
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During a late-February SSO proxy surge we observed a ~45m window where audit ingestion lag spiked and a concurrent signing certificate rotation created transient verification failures. The result was an intermittent 'log hole' where authenticated actions were recorded by some services but failed to reach the central audit index, causing gaps visible in compliance dashboards and failing a subset of downstream forensic queries. This ticket tracks the follow-up actions: automated detection for ingestion gaps, safe sequencing for signing/cert rotations, an ingest failover path, and retrospective replay tools for gap-fill.
timeline: 2026-02-25 03:12 UTC: SSO reverse-proxy autoscaler triggered (traffic spike from partner integration).
2026-02-25 03:20 UTC: Audit-forwarder queue depth begins to rise; first alert suppressed by rate-limiter.
2026-02-25 03:40 UTC: Automated cert-rotation job kicked off (scheduled maintenance window).
2026-02-25 03:45 UTC: Several forwarder workers restarted during rotation; some signed audit envelopes used old key material and were rejected by verifier.
2026-02-25 04:05 UTC: Backpressure propagated to upstream services; partial writes lingered in local buffers.
2026-02-25 04:50 UTC: Ingest backlog drained after manual scale-up and roll-forward; gaps identified in audit index and flagged by Compliance.
root_cause: Sequenced events: autoscaling surge + scheduled signing cert rotation overlapped, creating a window where newly signed envelopes used different key epochs than verifier expected.
Audit-forwarder lacked an end-to-end delivery confirmation and durable spill-to-disk fallback when downstream Kafka partitions lagged.
Monitoring thresholds were tuned for token loss but not for sequence continuity (no metric for 'first-seen id gaps').
impact_summary: ~12,000 audit entries delayed; estimated 2,100 entries missing from primary index during the window.
Compliance team escalated due to inability to produce contiguous trails for two enterprise customers during the period.
No evidence of tampering or data corruption; missing records persisted as 'not indexed' rather than altered.
mitigation_already_applied: Rolled forward the cert rotation to a single control-plane coordinator to avoid concurrent epoch flips.
Scaled audit-forwarder replicas by 3x and manually drained Kafka partitions; ran integrity check to pull dangling messages from spill queues.
Temporarily relaxed strict verifier epoch policy to accept a 5-minute grace window while we backfilled.
action_items: ENG-1: Implement 'gap-detector' metric and alert (owner: Claire Nguyen, ETA: 2026-03-12) - emit a continuous sequence check per-customer and route alerts to Security PagerDuty.
ENG-2: Add durable local spill-to-object-store for forwarder with retry/at-least-once replay (owner: Miguel Torres, ETA: 2026-04-02) - design doc and PoC PR referenced below.
ENG-3: Make cert rotation a two-phase canary (owner: Ravi Singh, ETA: 2026-03-22) - sequence: publish next-epoch publicly, wait >= rotation-grace, then flip; add preflight verifier checks.
ENG-4: Build idempotent replay tooling for compliance backfill and expose an audit-replay API for authorized SRE actions (owner: Asha Patel, ETA: 2026-03-28).
ENG-5: Emergency runbook update: include 'check cert-epoch drift' step and automatic temporary verifier-grace toggle for on-call (owner: Oncall Rotation, ETA: 2026-03-08).
ENG-6: Post-incident compliance report with sample-backed proofs and replayed indices for affected customers (owner: Compliance - Maria Lopez, ETA: 2026-03-18).
acceptance_criteria: gap-detector emits alerts for synthetic gap injection tests and on-call acknowledges within configured SLO (test plan in Confluence).
Forwarder can survive a downstream partition lag of 24 hours with zero tail-loss by spilling and replaying messages, validated in staging.
Cert-rotation canary completed twice in staging and one prod canary with no index gaps before general rollout.
Compliance can request and receive a fully reconstructed contiguous trail for the incident window via audit-replay API within 48 hours.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Introducing spill-to-OSS increases storage costs and operational complexity; will add retention policy and TTL to keep costs bounded.
Extending verifier grace reduces strictness of realtime verification for a short window — must be guarded by automated canary checks to avoid prolonged reduced guarantees.
Replay tooling requires careful authz to avoid exposing raw audit payloads; will integrate with existing RBAC and provide redaction options.

2026-03-08 - Oncall Rotation: Runbook updated and on-call notified; test page exercise scheduled for 2026-03-11 to validate detection and manual backfill steps.
